name: Question 3
problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}9{e}^{4t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)
$$

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=9u(t)+2v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(9{e}^{4t})^{′} \\ (2{e}^{2t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}36{e}^{4t} \\ 4{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

If u(t)=[e4t0] and v(t)=[0e2t] are solutions to x′(t)=Ax(t), find Aw(t) where w(t)=[9e4t2e2t].

a
Aw=[8e4t18e2t]
b
Aw=[36e2t4e4t]
c
Aw=[9e4t2e2t]
d
Aw=[8e2t18e4t]
e
Aw=[36e4t4e2t]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since u(t) and v(t) are solutions to x′(t)=Ax(t), the superposition principle guarantees that cu(t)+dv(t) is also a solution to x′(t)=Ax(t) for all c,d∈R.

Notice that w(t)=9u(t)+2v(t).

Therefore, w is a solution to x′(t)=Ax(t). So, in order to find Aw(t) we just need to find w′(t) as follows: Aw=w′(t)=[(9e4t)′(2e2t)′]=[36e4t4e2t].
